title: I built a free SDK that puts real AI inside any game, even games that already exist.
author: korro_ai
selftext:
https://reddit.com/link/1xjicgw/video/xio8qw4qgmyh1/player

Hi! I built **Kinloom**: a free, open-source tool that puts real AI inside any game.



The video is **real gameplay**. A model answers live, nothing is scripted.





# 🎮 What you see in the video



**Talk to anyone, even in old games**

In a Pokémon FireRed fan mod, the trainer answers whatever you type, accepts or refuses your bet, and the battle really starts.



**A sentence becomes a room**

In a Binding of Isaac mod, describe a room and you fight in it. A wish becomes a real item, with real stats.



**A village that remembers**

Do something terrible. Everyone saw it, word spreads, and a ten-year-old won't let it go.



**A suspect who cracks**

Show him the evidence: his trust drops, his story changes, and he confesses.



**Type it, it's built**

"*a lighthouse made of cheese*" → it appears on the island.





# ⚙️ How it works, in 3 steps



**1. Your game asks for something, with an example of the answer.**

Kinloom.create("an item found in a cave",

{"name": "Glowcap", "value": \[1, 50\], "story": "Found under a cold stone."}) 



The example says: I want a name, a value between 1 and 50, and a short story.



**2. Kinloom asks the AI, then checks the reply.**

Wrong shape? Number out of range? An action your game doesn't have? Refused. Your game only ever receives answers that fit.



**3. If there's no AI, the example is the answer.**

No key, no internet, a slow model: your game gets your example (or your own lines) instantly. It never freezes, never crashes.





# 🧰 What your game can ask for



\- **chat**: a real conversation with a character, streamed, in about 1 second

\- **say**: a line when something happens (a kill, a goal, a sunset), instantly

\- **decide**: a choice or numbers, every frame, instantly

\- **act**: the AI uses your game's own functions (give an item, open a door, start a fight), and only valid calls get through

\- **create**: content of any shape (items, quests, levels, names, dialogue trees)

\- **event**: who saw what, so rumors spread and characters hold grudges

\- **Voice**: characters can speak and listen, with the system voice when there's no key





# 💡 What you can build with it



\- **NPCs you can really talk to**: shopkeepers you haggle with, companions who remember your choices

\- **Quests and items made on the fly**, in the exact format your game needs

\- **A game master that builds the next room**, wave or level from how you play

\- **Rivals and enemies that pick a strategy every frame**: attack, block, flee

\- **Detective and interrogation games where suspects lie**, remember and crack

\- **Living towns where people gossip**, have opinions and remember what you did

\- **Commentators and announcers that react to the actual match**

\- **Mods for games that already exist**: add AI characters to a game you didn't make





# 🧩 Works everywhere



\- Engines: Unity, Godot, JavaScript, C++, Rust, Java, Lua, Python



\- AI models: Claude, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio… or none at all



\- **No dependencies**: one file to drop into your project



\- **Ready to ship**: a relay keeps your API key off players' machines, with rate limits and spending caps





# ✨ Made for vibe coding



**pip install kinloom**

**cd your-game**

**kinloom init**



kinloom init finds your engine, adds Kinloom, and teaches your coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI…) how to use it.



Then just ask in plain words:

▎ "*Add a blacksmith I can talk to, who gives items to people she likes.*"



It picks the right calls and wires everything.





# 📊 Measured, not promised



\- Coding agents wrote working code 88% of the time with Kinloom, vs 8% without

\- Replies start in about 1 second, for about $0.0005 each

\- 45 attacks on a character's secret (prompt injection, fake authority…): the secret was kept
